issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify Animal.messageOnFeed() as returning a String, but the solution implements Animal.messageOnFeed() to return a FeedResponse object (and introduces FeedResponse). This is a structural return-type mismatch and will confuse students about the required method signature and expected usage of messageOnFeed().
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method return type consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement and UML to specify that messageOnFeed() returns a FeedResponse and document the FeedResponse class and its purpose, or (B) change the solution to have messageOnFeed() return a String (and remove FeedResponse), adjusting the solution subclasses and Farm usage accordingly. Prefer updating the solution to match the current problem spec (return String) unless FeedResponse is intentionally required and documented in the assignment.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify that Animal.messageOnFeed() returns a String, but the solution introduces a FeedResponse type and implements messageOnFeed() to return FeedResponse. This creates a mismatch: students are instructed to implement messageOnFeed() with a String return type, while the reference solution and concrete animal classes use FeedResponse. The divergence in the method's return type (String vs FeedResponse) is a conceptual inconsistency that can confuse students about the expected contract and what to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method contract across all artifacts. Either (a) update the problem statement and UML to specify that messageOnFeed() returns FeedResponse and document the FeedResponse class, or (b) change the solution to have messageOnFeed() return String (and adapt FeedResponse usage accordingly). Ensure template, problem statement, and solution use the same return type so students have a single clear target to implement.
